title: What is Collectors.collectingAndThen(downstream, finisher), and what are its typical uses (wrapping in unmodifiableList, extracting a value, converting the type)?
shortTitle: Collectors.collectingAndThen: wrap result, extract value, transform collected container
keyPoints: collectingAndThen runs a downstream collector and then applies a finisher transformation to the result
Classic use: collectingAndThen(toList(), Collections::unmodifiableList) makes the result read-only
Useful for extracting values: collectingAndThen(maxBy(comp), opt -> opt.orElseThrow()) unwraps Optional
Useful for type conversion: collectingAndThen(toList(), List::size) returns the count as the collected result
Works as a downstream inside groupingBy to produce clean per-group results
Java 10+ toUnmodifiableList() replaces the common unmodifiable-list use case
The finisher Function runs AFTER the downstream collector completes

s1_definition.oneliner: collectingAndThen applies a finisher transformation after the downstream collector completes, wrapping, unwrapping, or converting the collected result in one step.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Signature** – `collectingAndThen(Collector<T,?,R1> downstream, Function<R1,R2> finisher)`.
- **Behavior** – the downstream collector collects normally; then the finisher transforms the result.
- **Wrapping** – `collectingAndThen(toList(), Collections::unmodifiableList)` makes the list read-only.
- **Unwrapping** – `collectingAndThen(maxBy(comp), opt -> opt.orElseThrow())` extracts the value from Optional.
- **Converting** – `collectingAndThen(toList(), List::size)` returns the size instead of the list.
s1_definition.analogy: collectingAndThen is like a post office: you collect all the letters (downstream collector), then stamp and seal the envelope (finisher). One operation handles both the collection and the final packaging.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  collectingAndThen(toList(), Collections::unmodifiableList):

  Stream: "TRD-001" → "TRD-002" → "TRD-003"
              │           │           │
              ▼           ▼           ▼
  Downstream (toList):
    ["TRD-001", "TRD-002", "TRD-003"]
              │
              ▼
  Finisher (unmodifiableList):
    UnmodifiableList["TRD-001", "TRD-002", "TRD-003"]
              │
              ▼
  .add("X") → UnsupportedOperationException
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
collectingAndThen applies a finisher transformation after the downstream collector completes. The three primary uses are wrapping (make the result unmodifiable), unwrapping (extract a value from Optional returned by maxBy/minBy), and converting (collect to list, finisher converts to array or counts size).

It is especially useful as a downstream inside groupingBy to produce clean per-group results without post-processing. Java 10+ `toUnmodifiableList()` replaces the most common use case, but collectingAndThen remains the general tool for any arbitrary finisher.

Remember one sentence: collectingAndThen runs a collector then applies a finisher, useful for wrapping, unwrapping, or converting the collected result in one step.
